entries.text: At 29° Virgo, mastery means knowing when the work is complete—not perfect, but complete. The most powerful edit is often deletion. The strongest boundary is sometimes an ending. The greatest service might be modeling what sustainable caring looks like.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.structuralFunction: paragraph under How to Work With This Eclipse (Hint: You Kinda Don't)
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: The rest is tomorrow's work. And as the equinox reminds us, tomorrow's light will be perfectly balanced with tomorrow's darkness, there's no rush to do it all in today's light.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.structuralFunction: paragraph under How to Work With This Eclipse (Hint: You Kinda Don't)

entries.text: Between now and February 2027, everything about how you work, serve, care for yourself, and structure your days is getting dismantled and rebuilt from scratch. This isn't a renovation where you keep the foundation. This is bulldozers and blank slates.

entries.text: You know that schedule that would kill a normal person? The one where you're everyone's emergency contact but no one's priority? Dead. Done. This Solar Eclipse in your 6th house is torching your exhausting routines while Mercury in your partnership sector can't get a straight answer from anyone.

entries.text: The eclipse at 29° Virgo is the universe's way of saying "enough." Mars enters Scorpio tomorrow in your 8th house, so those band-aid solutions you've been slapping on everything? They're about to get ripped off. No more surface fixes. No more pretending you're fine, this is fine. You're going deep.

entries.text: Saturn retrograde in your 12th house has been showing you exactly how you became your own worst enemy. That voice that says you're only valuable when you're producing? It's not your motivator. It's your abuser. And you're the one keeping it employed.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: You don't have to earn rest through exhaustion. You don't have to collapse to deserve a break. Stop treating burnout like it's a badge of honor. It's not. It's just burnout.
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.text: If they need you to destroy yourself to be useful to them, they don't need you. They need an assistant. And last time I checked, you weren't hired for that position (and if you were, you need a raise).

entries.text: This eclipse is hitting your creativity and joy sector at the same time Venus is moving through there. Think of it like this: the universe is forcing you to look at what actually makes you happy versus what you've been pretending brings you joy.

entries.text: For years, you've been sitting on creative projects because they're "not ready yet." You've been the stable, calm one in relationships while stuffing down what you really feel. Maybe you've been working on "anger management" while everyone else gets to push your buttons without consequences. This eclipse in your 5th house is done watching you suffer.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Mars entering Scorpio in your partnership sector tomorrow means those dynamics you've been managing while biting your tongue are about to get real uncomfortable. Mercury in your 6th house is trying to help you communicate your daily needs and health, but the truth is, you've been suppressing them for so long you might not even know what they are anymore.

entries.text: Uranus retrograde in Gemini in your 2nd house since September 6 is asking you to reconsider what you value. Not what you think you should value - what actually matters to you. This eclipse might force some of those decisions.

entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: The question isn't whether you're good enough to share your creativity or be loved as you are. If they'll love the edited version of you. Show them the director's cut anyway. Your mess IS the art. Your chaos IS the creation.

entries.text: Let me guess - you're the family IT department, therapist, and general fixer-upper, organizing everyone's life while yours is held together with duct tape and denial. This eclipse in your home sector is revoking your lifetime membership to the ‘fix everyone's problems, but yours comes last club’.

entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: The 29° eclipse is ending a chapter with your living situation or family dynamics. With Mars entering Scorpio tomorrow in your 6th house, the daily routines that emerge from these changes will be intense but necessary. Mercury, your ruler, in your 5th house is trying to help you have fun, but it's opposing Saturn and Neptune. You can't even remember what fun feels like because you've been too busy managing everyone else's drama (including yours). Your daily life is about to reflect these family pattern changes whether you're ready or not.

entries.text: Uranus retrograde in your sign is the identity crisis you've been avoiding. You've been playing so many roles for so many people, you don't know which one is actually you. Spoiler: maybe none of them. When Uranus slides back into Taurus and your 12th house on November 7, unconscious patterns will surface.

entries.text: Saturn retrograde in Pisces in your 10th house through November is showing you how family patterns show up in your professional life. That need to fix everything? It started at home, or because of your home life.

entries.text: Venus in Virgo in your home sector isn't about creating the perfect space. It's about creating a space where you can be imperfect safely. Stop organizing your space to avoid feeling your feelings. You don't have to fix their problems to earn your place at the table. You belong there even if you show up empty-handed and needing help yourself.

entries.text: This Solar Eclipse in Virgo shakes up your 3rd house of communication and daily life while Mercury in Libra in your 4th house creates confusion about home and family through oppositions to Saturn and Neptune. This eclipse is cutting the power to your mental hamster wheel, and it's about time.

entries.text: The 29° Virgo eclipse is done with your overthinking. With Mars entering Scorpio tomorrow in your 5th house of creativity and romance, you're about to discover what happens when you feel instead of analyze.

entries.text: With your ruler Venus moving into your sign October 13, you'll integrate what this eclipse reveals. But right now? Let the unconscious become conscious. If you're still perfecting yourself in private, ask yourself: what am I preparing for that never seems to arrive?

entries.text: The Pisces New Moon at 7:45 PM EST on February 27 is a deep pull into the abyss. A lunar doorway into the unseen, the forgotten, the ancestral tides that exist beneath waking consciousness. The water is dark here, bottomless.

entries.text: This is the last New Moon of the astrological year, a final exhale before the Sun crosses into Aries and ignites the next cycle. In Pisces, the sign of boundlessness, this lunation is an invitation to step beyond logic, beyond form, into the unseen. It calls us into the dreamtime, the liminal, the space between endings and beginnings.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Pisces is the last sign. The end of the road. It erodes the edges of things, wears them down until they are shapeless, formless, impossible to hold onto. It is the dream that dissolves upon waking, the cycle that closes without ceremony. This is the point where you let go. Not because you want to, but because you don’t have a choice.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Pisces is mutable water, the shifting tide, the deep well, the mist that obscures and reveals. Its ruler, Neptune, governs the intangible: intuition, imagination, illusion, and surrender. Unlike other New Moons, which often feel like a starting point, this one is a portal, a passageway between what was and what will be.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: But you don’t get to simply float here. Not this time. Saturn is watching.
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.text: And let’s be honest, you already know what this is about. You’ve been avoiding it. Letting it drift just out of reach. Hoping it would dissolve on its own. But it hasn’t, has it? Saturn is sitting right here, pulling it back into focus.
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.text: I could tell you to set intentions, to manifest, to plant seeds. But that’s not what this is for. This isn’t a garden. It’s a funeral. It’s the moment where you stop pretending you don’t see what’s slipping away. The moment where you stand at the shore and watch the tide pull it under, knowing it’s never coming back.

entries.text: This lunation is not soft. Not in the way we like to romanticize Pisces as a dreamer’s sign, a gentle tide of imagination and wonder. No, this is Pisces in its highest and densest forms. This is Pisces with five planets drowning in its waters, answering to Neptune itself, standing at the last degree of its own sign.
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.text: Everything in this chart answers to Neptune, the great dissolver, the omnipresent force of dream and disillusionment. Neptune moves toward 29º Pisces, a degree of endings, of finality. The last stretch of its transit through the sign it rules. Whatever unravels now is not a mistake. It is part of the larger dissolution.

entries.text: This is not Neptune’s usual dreamscape, not the soft-focus blur of past years. Neptune is still here, at 28° Pisces, but Saturn has taken over. Neptune is fading. Saturn is sharpening the outline. And then there’s Mercury at 24° Pisces, drifting through these waters, dissolving the certainty of words, making everything feel just out of reach. You may struggle to articulate what you’re feeling. But you don’t need to. You already know.
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.text: You should know, I hated writing the last few paragraphs. But here we are. And maybe you hate reading it too, because you already know where it’s going. And trust me, I get it. Somewhere in your life, you are hitting a wall that cannot be bypassed. This New Moon makes it impossible to ignore.

entries.text: At its highest vibration, this is a lunation of vision, prophecy, divine surrender. To trust the unknown, to move without sight but with faith. To let the old self dissolve in the tide and allow the next one to emerge, untouched by past definitions.

entries.text: At its lowest, this is a lunation of confusion, escapism, and deception. A drowning in illusion, a false vision, a mirage that vanishes as soon as you try to grasp it. A choice between intuition and delusion. Between transcendence and avoidance.

entries.text: Lilith in Libra sits across from this lunation like a shadow at the edge of the room. Pisces wants to dissolve, to blur the edges. But Lilith refuses to let you look away. Pisces likes to dissolve, to blur the edges, but Lilith cuts through the fog and shows you exactly what you’ve been avoiding. It’s about accountability. It’s about where you’ve given too much of yourself away. Where you’ve sacrificed too much for the illusion of peace.

entries.text: Lilith in Libra forces the question: What have you been tolerating that you should have burned down a long time ago? Where has your desire for peace left you powerless? And more importantly, why did you let it happen?

entries.text: Libra seeks harmony, but Lilith in Libra does not settle for false balance. If something has been unjust, this opposition calls it to the surface. The quiet resentment, the exhaustion of maintaining appearances, the places where you have compromised yourself for the sake of keeping the peace. Lilith is here to make sure you see them.

This Mars doesn’t seek out conflict, but it will burn down the whole house if something threatens what it loves. If something is leaving your life, this Mars teaches you to release it with quiet strength.

entries.text: Think back to March 2011, when Neptune first entered Pisces. That was the beginning of this era. What dreams have you been living under? What illusions have you clung to? This New Moon is where the dream ends, or shifts into something real. So if there is something you need to let go of, do it now. Because once the fires of Aries come, there won't be time to grieve.

entries.text: There is something shifting beneath your awareness. A presence just beyond your periphery. This New Moon lands in your twelfth house of endings, surrender, and the subconscious. The place where things go to die, or transform. This is where ghosts reside, where unfinished business lingers, where the weight of what is unspoken grows heavy. The past is knocking. The dreams you tried to forget are surfacing. Saturn is here now. The illusions you’ve lived under won’t survive this. You cannot out-run, out-fight, or out-perform this.

entries.text: You may feel a pull toward isolation, a need to retreat into yourself. But Saturn is watching. You cannot outrun your own subconscious. The structures you have built to contain these hidden parts of yourself will not hold forever. What have you been avoiding? What must be confronted before the next chapter begins?

entries.text: Lilith in Libra moves through your 7th house, unsettling your relationships, drawing out tensions that have long simmered beneath the surface. Have you compromised too much? Have you settled for balance at the cost of truth? The way you engage with others is shifting. The masks you’ve worn in partnerships, romantic, business, or otherwise, are slipping. This lunation will not allow you to pretend any longer.

entries.text: Mars in Cancer, forming a trine to this lunation, reminds you that some fights are fought in silence. Mars activates your 4th house of home, ancestry, and emotional security, urging you to protect what is sacred, to reclaim your inner foundation. Not all battles require aggression, some demand stillness, patience, and a willingness to sit in discomfort. If the past is calling, will you answer?

entries.text: The Pisces New Moon is dissolving something. An old story. A long-buried fear. A version of yourself that no longer belongs. Sit with it. Do not fight it. The more you resist, the heavier it becomes. Something is ending. But that means something new is waiting beyond it. Let it go. Whatever “it” is, you already know.

entries.text: The people who were once your home may no longer feel like home. The places where you once felt seen may now feel foreign (literally). This New Moon lands in your eleventh house of community, dreams, and alliances. Something is shifting here, and not in a way you can control. The friend group, the network, the collective vision you were a part of... something is dissolving. Saturn is showing you the truth: who is real, who is not. Lilith is forcing the question: What have you tolerated for the sake of belonging?

entries.text: Lilith in Libra lingers in your 6th house, casting a shadow over your daily routines, work, and health. Have you been overextending yourself, trying to meet unrealistic expectations? Where have you compromised your well-being for the sake of keeping things running smoothly? This lunation will make it clear: balance must be restored. If your habits have become self-sacrificing rather than sustaining, it’s time to reclaim your time and energy.

entries.text: Saturn is cutting through the fog, making it clear where you’ve been drifting instead of deciding. If your path is shifting, let it. You don’t have to keep performing a version of yourself that you’ve outgrown. But be warned: Neptune’s illusions do not go quietly. You may feel disoriented, uncertain, untethered. That is Saturn doing its job. Let the false dream die. What remains is real. And that is what you will build from.

entries.text: The Pisces New Moon floods your eighth house, the underworld of intimacy, shared resources, power, and loss. You are standing in the liminal now, face-to-face with what you owe, not just financially, but karmically. What is left unfinished? What patterns keep cycling through your relationships, your fears, your intimacy? The fears you keep buried, the debts that linger from past choices, the wounds that keep reopening, you cannot ignore them now. The ghosts of past choices come to collect. the fears you’ve buried, the contracts you’ve outgrown, the ties that still bind. Saturn does not allow unfinished business. If you have given too much, it’s time to reclaim what is yours. If you have taken more than you should, the scales will balance. The weight must be released. The debt must be settled. What is leaving will not return. Carry nothing forward that was never meant to be yours.

entries.text: The Pisces New Moon stirs the waters of your 2nd house, the house of worth, resources, and what you claim as yours. But Pisces does not cling. It does not count coins or build walls. It dissolves. And under this lunation, something you have held tightly, an attachment, an expectation, a belief about what you need is slipping away.

entries.text: This is not just about money. This is about what you have assigned value to. The things, the people, the roles you have anchored yourself to, are they sustaining you, or are they keeping you tethered to an old version of yourself? Saturn is watching. And Saturn does not let you evade the truth. Lilith in Libra lingers in your 9th house, casting a shadow over what you believe. Where have you accepted someone else’s version of reality? Where have you silenced yourself to fit into a framework that was never yours? This lunation will make the imbalance undeniable.

entries.text: And then there is Mars in Cancer, forming a trine to this lunation, reminding you that some endings are not a failure but a reclamation. Some battles are won not through force but through release. The more you resist this dissolution, the more it will take. Surrender is not weakness. It is knowing when to stop gripping something that is already gone. Think back to March 2011, when Neptune first entered Pisces. What did you believe then about security, about ownership, about what it means to be stable? This New Moon is the reckoning of that vision. If something is meant to remain, it will. If not, let it go before it becomes a weight too heavy to carry.

Pisces is the last sign. The end of the road. And you are feeling it now, the weight of something being washed away. This lunation is not asking you to become someone new. It is asking you to remember who you were before the world told you who to be.

entries.text: Lilith in Libra lingers in your 8th house, casting a shadow over what you have shared, what you have merged, what you have sacrificed. What parts of yourself have you given away in the name of closeness? Where have you compromised your truth for the sake of harmony? Lilith does not let you look away. This lunation will make the imbalance clear. And then there is Mars in Cancer, forming a trine to this lunation, reminding you that transformation is not always fire and fury. Some shifts happen in the quiet. Some battles are won by simply walking away. Some versions of you must be left behind. Think back to March 2011, when Neptune first entered Pisces. What dreams did you have for yourself then? What illusions did you build your identity around? This New Moon is the final chapter of that vision. If it was never real, let it dissolve. If it was, let it become something stronger.

The Sun enters Pisces on February 18, 2025, shifting the collective frequency into the ineffable. The dreamscape thickens, the boundaries blur. Time bends. This is the season of surrender. Where structure loosens, and what is unseen makes itself known.

This is not about control. It never was. It is the tide that takes what it will and leaves behind only what was meant to last. This is where you let go. This is where you let the ocean decide.

entries.text: The Sun in Pisces draws us into a liminal space, a place between reality and dream. This transit blurs the lines between self and other, logic and intuition, the seen and the unseen. It’s a call to float, to surrender, to allow. Pisces is mutable water, a tide that erases footprints, a wave that washes away what no longer holds weight. It softens the structures we cling to, dissolves the borders we’ve drawn, reminding us that nothing is as solid as we pretend it to be.

entries.text: This is a season of endings. Unfinished business rises like driftwood, fragments of old stories washing ashore. Under Pisces, we don’t move forward by force, we feel our way there, trusting the pull of the unseen. It’s a time for divination, music, poetry, and solitude. It’s also a time when illusions can thicken, when boundaries can dissolve too far, when reality feels like mist slipping through our fingers. And just as we step into these shifting tides, Venus forms a minor square to Uranus, sending ripples of unease through the waters. Restlessness may arise. Longing for change. But for now, we float, letting the current decide.

entries.text: After two months of retrograde motion, Mars stations direct at 17° Cancer on February 23. Since Mars entered retrograde in December 2024, we’ve been retracing our steps, examining where our energy has been drained, where old battles have left scars, where we’ve been clinging to outdated modes of defense. Mars in Cancer fights in a different way, it doesn’t charge forward, it protects. It defends. It moves through emotion rather than logic, acting from the gut rather than the mind. Cancer, ruled by the Moon, is the sign of the home, the past, and ancestral memory. Here, Mars does not wield its sword, but rather guards the gates of the heart, fights for safety, and defends emotional territory.

entries.text: During the retrograde, we’ve been dragged back through old battlefields, forced to revisit wounds that never quite healed, to question whether our instincts to fight, flee, or fortify have been serving us. Where have we exhausted ourselves defending something no longer worth the fight? Where have we built walls that now trap us rather than protect us?

entries.text: Cancer is cardinal water, it initiates, but it does so through feeling, through intuition, through deep undercurrents that move unseen until they surge forth. Mars in Cancer reminds us that not all battles are won through brute force. Some wars are won by knowing when to fight, when to retreat, and when to let the tide wash it all away.

entries.text: Mars remains in its post-retrograde shadow until May 2, meaning we will be integrating these lessons for months to come. The last time Mars stationed direct in Cancer after a retrograde was April 2008, when it turned direct at 24° Gemini before re-entering Cancer in early May. However, if we are looking for the last full Mars retrograde that ended in Cancer, we must go back further, to March 1991, when Mars stationed direct at 12° Cancer, its armor waterlogged, its fire reduced to embers.

entries.text: This is the last New Moon of the astrological year, a final exhale before the Sun crosses into Aries and ignites the next cycle. In Pisces, the sign of boundlessness, this lunation is an invitation to step beyond logic, beyond form, into the unseen. It calls us into the dreamtime, the liminal, the space between endings and beginnings.

entries.text: Pisces is the last sign. The end of the road. It erodes the edges of things, wears them down until they are shapeless, formless, impossible to hold onto. It is the dream that dissolves upon waking, the cycle that closes without ceremony. This is the point where you let go. Not because you want to, but because you don’t have a choice.

entries.text: Pisces is mutable water, the shifting tide, the deep well, the mist that obscures and reveals. Its ruler, Neptune, governs the intangible: intuition, imagination, illusion, and surrender. Unlike other New Moons, which often feel like a starting point, this one is a portal, a passageway between what was and what will be.

entries.text: And let’s be honest, you already know what this is about. You’ve been avoiding it. Letting it drift just out of reach. Hoping it would dissolve on its own. But it hasn’t, has it? Saturn is sitting right here, pulling it back into focus.

entries.text: I could tell you to set intentions, to manifest, to plant seeds. But that’s not what this is for. This isn’t a garden. It’s a funeral. It’s the moment where you stop pretending you don’t see what’s slipping away. The moment where you stand at the shore and watch the tide pull it under, knowing it’s never coming back.

entries.text: This is a heavier Pisces New Moon than we’ve had before. It’s not Neptune’s usual dreamscape, not the soft-focus blur of past years. Neptune is still here, at 28° Pisces, but Saturn has taken over. Neptune is fading. Saturn is sharpening the outline. And then there’s Mercury at 24° Pisces, drifting through these waters, dissolving the certainty of words, making everything feel just out of reach. You may struggle to articulate what you’re feeling. But you don’t need to. You already know.

entries.text: You should know, I hated writing the last few paragraphs. But here we are. And maybe you hate reading it too, because you already know where it’s going. And trust me, I get it. Somewhere in your life, you are hitting a wall that cannot be bypassed. This New Moon makes it impossible to ignore.

entries.text: Lilith in Libra sits across from this lunation like a shadow at the edge of the room. Pisces wants to dissolve, to blur the edges. But Lilith refuses to let you look away. Pisces likes to dissolve, to blur the edges, but Lilith cuts through the fog and shows you exactly what you’ve been avoiding. It’s about accountability. It’s about where you’ve given too much of yourself away. Where you’ve sacrificed too much for the illusion of peace.

entries.text: Venus in Aries does not negotiate. She doesn’t ask for permission. She doesn’t soften her edges to be palatable. She wants what she wants, and she wants it now. But when retrograde, that fire turns inward. The urgency doesn’t disappear, it just circles, looping through the past... old desires, old lovers, old wounds that refuse to cauterize. Aries is ruled by Mars, and Mars is not sentimental. So if you think this retrograde is going to be about nostalgia, about sweetly revisiting the past to find closure, think again. This is war magick. A moment of clarity with the self. A confrontation with how you have fought for love, or failed to.

entries.text: Then the retreat. Pisces. The battlefield dissolves into fog. Aries is direct action, but Pisces is the dream. The undoing. The love that slips through your fingers. What does Venus retrograde in Pisces bring? The love that never quite ended, the love that never quite materialized. The illusion of sacrifice, the self-delusion of martyrdom. Venus is exalted in Pisces, but in retrograde, she’s not quite herself. She second-guesses. She wonders if the sacrifice was worth it. She revisits the places she left herself behind.

entries.text: Eight years ago, 2017. A cycle completing itself, or reopening. You should know: Venus retrograde is not just about romance. It’s about worth. What you once believed you deserved. What you settled for. Here’s the thing about Venus retrograde: it reveals. It strips away the illusion, the justifications, the pretty lies you tell yourself about love, about worth, about what is and isn’t possible. And once you see, you can’t unsee. That’s the point.

entries.text: So. What did 2017 teach you? What patterns are repeating? What love stories, heartbreaks, and self-worth lessons remain unfinished? The past is knocking, and it’s inside the house.

entries.text: As we drift in Pisces' dreamscape, Mercury enters Aries on March 3, igniting thoughts, words, and ideas like sparks against dry tinder. Here, words move fast, ideas hit hard, and filters disappear. Mercury in Aries isn’t interested in pleasantries, it cuts to the chase, speaks before thinking, and doesn’t wait for permission.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.structuralFunction: paragraph under March 3-29: Mercury in Aries
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: This transit brings a sense of urgency, a need to say what’s been left unsaid, a push to initiate conversations that might otherwise linger too long in the background. But urgency is not always clarity. Sometimes it’s just heat, just impulse, just reaction. Mercury in Aries is a powerful tool when wielded with intention, but when left unchecked, it can ignite arguments, burn bridges, and speak truths that aren’t totally fully formed yet.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.structuralFunction: paragraph under March 3-29: Mercury in Aries
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: But Mercury’s journey through Aries comes with a caveat, it will retrograde at 9° Aries on March 15. This means whatever begins in early March will be up for review. Words spoken in passion may need to be retracted. Ideas launched prematurely may need to be reworked. Actions taken impulsively may lead to dead ends.
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: This is not a reason to silence yourself. Aries isn’t here to be small. But it is a reminder that not everything needs to be said just because it can be. That sometimes, the most powerful thing we can do with our words is let them breathe before setting them loose.

entries.text: Eclipses bring fated events, sudden shifts, and doors closing permanently. This one is particularly potent. It’s the second eclipse in a series along the Virgo-Pisces axis (2024-2027), continuing a storyline that began with the Pisces Lunar Eclipse on September 17, 2024.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.structuralFunction: paragraph under March 14: Total Lunar Eclipse in Virgo
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Virgo is precision, order, and function. Pisces is fluidity, chaos, and transcendence. This eclipse asks us to balance the two; to integrate the dream with the tangible, to surrender while still keeping our feet on the ground.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.structuralFunction: paragraph under March 14: Total Lunar Eclipse in Virgo
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: What is being revealed? What structures must shift? What illusions must fall away? Expect major revelations in the areas of health, work, daily routines, and spiritual integration. The Virgo Moon is relentlessly practical, and under its light, we will see exactly what needs to change.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.structuralFunction: paragraph under March 14: Total Lunar Eclipse in Virgo
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Pisces Sun, Saturn pressing close. Neptune at the threshold, 29 degrees, the last breath before the abyss. This is not a dream. This is consequence. The last time you stood here, you had illusions to cling to. Now? Just the raw truth, stripped bare. The story you’ve been telling yourself—about who you are, about what you can endure—falters under the weight of its own contradictions.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.structuralFunction: paragraph under March 14: Total Lunar Eclipse in Virgo
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Jupiter in Gemini, words expanding and multiplying, but do they mean anything? Mercury in Aries, blunt, impatient. You could say something. You could say everything. Would it change what needs to be faced?
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.text: Chiron, 21 Aries. The wound that does not close. The place where you keep returning, like a tongue to a broken tooth. The wound does not define you, but the way you carry it does. You cannot keep living in the echo of an injury.
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.text: Pluto in Aquarius, still near the gate. Revolution is inevitable, but slow. You want finality. You want a clean break. Pluto does not grant that mercy. Change will come, but it will not be neat. It will not be comfortable. You will not leave this eclipse unmarked.

entries.text: Uranus, 24 degrees Taurus, rattling the foundations. If you haven’t made the change willingly, it will be made for you. Venus and Mars, both caught in their own entanglements, one eager, one hesitant. The heart and the body want different things. Which do you listen to?

entries.text: Lilith at 28 Libra. The rejection of pleasing. This eclipse asks: who are you when you stop trying to be digestible? What happens when you stand in your own darkness and do not apologize?
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.structuralFunction: paragraph under March 14: Total Lunar Eclipse in Virgo

entries.text: And then there’s the axis. The North Node at 27 Pisces, the South Node at 27 Virgo. The known, the unknown. The familiar patterns, the dissolution of them. The past calls, begging for resolution, for comfort, for routine. The future stands before you, liquid and uncertain. You already know what needs to be done. The eclipse simply forces your hand.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.structuralFunction: paragraph under March 14: Total Lunar Eclipse in Virgo
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: This is the crossroads. This is the point of no return. The shadows only look ominous because you have been staring at the light too long. Let the darkness settle. Let it show you what is real. And when the Moon emerges again, it will not be the world that has changed. It will be you.

entries.text: Just a day after the eclipse, Mercury stations retrograde at 9° Aries. The fiery momentum we’ve built suddenly stalls. This is not a time to push forward but to go back.

entries.text: Mercury Rx in Aries revisits battles, reopens old wounds, and forces us to rethink impulsive decisions. This retrograde asks us to go back over our words, our decisions, our impulses. To make sure what we’ve started is actually what we want.

entries.text: What words need to be retracted? What ideas need refining? What actions need reconsideration?

entries.text: This retrograde will extend until April 7, after which Mercury will move back into Pisces on April 16 for a final dive into intuition before fully exiting Aries on May 10. That means whatever comes up now will take time to sort itself out. By April 16, Mercury will retreat into Pisces, bringing a final opportunity to process, reflect, and approach things from a more intuitive lens. But by May 10, when Mercury finally exits its post-retrograde shadow, we’ll be moving forward with full clarity on what we truly mean vs. what was just heat in the moment. Take your time. Slow down. Think before you speak. Because what’s said now will be remembered later.

entries.text: You blaze forward, always. But Pisces season is a slow tide eroding urgency, a dream state thick with old ghosts. The road ahead is fogged over, and no matter how fast you run, the destination dissolves in the mist. This is a time to pause, to listen, to let the current move you instead of fighting against it.

entries.text: With Mars stationing direct in Cancer on February 23, you feel the weight of unprocessed emotions pulling at your gut. Let them surface. You may feel especially protective of your home and those you love, yet old wounds from childhood or family dynamics may surface, demanding attention. Be mindful of passive-aggression or defensive reactions—true healing happens when you face the discomfort directly.
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.text: The Pisces New Moon on February 27 reveals what must be surrendered; old habits of control, buried grief, subconscious defenses. It’s a time to release expectations and trust the unknown. By the time Mercury enters your sign on March 3, your voice sharpens, your thoughts quicken. Then comes the Virgo Eclipse on March 14, spotlighting your routines, your work, your body. If you’ve been running yourself ragged, the eclipse will intervene. Where has self-neglect crept in? If something no longer sustains you—whether a job, habit, or commitment; it will be stripped away. Rest is not a weakness. Adaptation is a form of strength.

entries.text: Venus begins this descent in Aries, lighting up your sixth house of routine, work, and the body. A strange place for love, but then again, you have never been the kind to separate romance from survival. You have fought for love before. You have bled for it. But was it worth it? Did you mistake the fight for the feeling? Venus in Aries does not beg. She does not negotiate. If your love has required a war, this retrograde forces you to ask if it was ever love at all.

entries.text: Mercury stations retrograde in Aries on March 15, just after a total Lunar Eclipse in Virgo. You will be forced to reconsider the battles you are picking. Not every fight needs to be won. Some are better left to drown. This is the final tide before Aries season. Let it take what no longer belongs. Let it soften the parts of you that cannot survive the fire ahead.

entries.text: Pisces season is an ocean of longing, calling you deeper into the world of dreams, but not all dreams are meant to last. Some dissolve like seafoam, leaving only the lesson behind. Who do you trust? Who truly sees you? The New Moon on February 27 asks you to release illusions: about friendships, about community, about the vision of your future that no longer holds.

entries.text: With Mars stationing direct, you might find long-standing tensions in friendships or group dynamics coming to the forefront. This is a time to reassess who you align with. Are your ideals still in sync, or have you outgrown them? Some partings may be necessary.

entries.text: Venus retrograde does not bring simple answers. It does not soothe. It does not make peace. It disrupts. It reveals. In Aries, Venus moves through your fifth house... love, pleasure, risk. The past comes calling, but this time, you are seeing it for what it really was. Old lovers, old passions, old versions of yourself. The things you once desired. The things you once thought were love. Aries does not hesitate. Venus in Aries is now, now, now, except in retrograde, she is spinning in circles, moving forward only to return to the same place again. Venus then moves into Pisces. And suddenly, the illusion cracks. The past softens, but it does not disappear. This is the love that slipped through your fingers. The longing that never quite left. The person you thought you had let go of but never really did. The sacrifice you once made, was it worth it? Or did you abandon yourself in the process?

entries.text: By the Virgo Eclipse on March 14, the focus shifts to your creative life. What have you been creating for others rather than for yourself? What joy has been lost under obligation? This eclipse demands a dismantling. Not everything stable is worth holding onto. If a romance or passion project has felt stagnant, expect a shift. Realignment is necessary.

entries.text: Your career path bends in strange directions now. Pisces season makes everything uncertain, from your professional goals to your public image. What once seemed like a clear plan is suddenly blurred at the edges. Neptune rules this domain for you, and under its influence, not everything is what it seems. The professional path you’ve been walking, the roles you’ve played, the titles you’ve carried, the goals you once swore would define you... suddenly shifting. The destination isn’t gone, but the map you were following no longer makes sense. Neptune has been casting its spell over your career sector for over a decade, shaping dreams, illusions, and sometimes delusions about what success should look like. Under its influence, things are not always what they seem. The offers that appear promising may be empty. The doubts creeping in may not be paranoia, but instinct. What if the version of success you’re striving for isn’t actually yours?

entries.text: The Pisces New Moon on February 27 asks for a surrender. Not defeat, not failure, just surrender. To let go of the outdated ambition, the title that no longer fits, the external validation that once felt essential. If you’ve been pushing forward at the expense of your well-being, this is where the course correction begins. Pay attention to hidden power dynamics at work: someone may not be as supportive as they seem. Pay attention to what is implied rather than said, promised rather than given. Pisces thrives in subtlety, but Saturn is here too, demanding clarity. Where do you stand? And who stands with you?

entries.text: By the Virgo Eclipse on March 14, attention turns to home. Work-life balance is no longer a theoretical discussion.. it’s a demand. What structures need to shift so that you are not running on empty? What must be rebuilt from the ground up? If your living situation feels unstable, this eclipse may bring a necessary change. Some Geminis may relocate, redefine family roles, or make career shifts that prioritize personal well-being over professional ambition. Pisces season asks you to trust the currents, not the map.

entries.text: You've likely felt exhausted, emotionally raw, or stuck in old wounds you thought you had already healed. Mars has been dragging you backward through old battlefields, forcing you to sit in the wreckage, to feel the weight of wounds you swore had healed. Exhaustion has set in, not just in your body, but in your spirit. You have been fighting ghosts, wrestling with shadows. But on February 23, Mars stations direct at 17° in your sign, and the dam finally breaks. Memories resurface, emotions hit like a tide, lessons return like old debts coming due. This is an unbinding, a breaking open. The weight you’ve carried begins to shift, but not before you acknowledge why it was there in the first place.

entries.text: Pisces season does not offer clean resolutions. It does not hand you closure tied up in a neat bow. Instead, it urges you to go deeper. To sit with the unraveling. To trust the places where the ground gives way beneath you.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: And then, February 27, the Pisces New Moon. A reset. A portal. An invitation. Pisces rules your ninth house, the domain of belief, knowledge, and the stories you tell yourself about the world. This lunation asks you to reconnect with your own intuition, your own wisdom, your own sense of truth. The way forward is not logical, it is felt. But Neptune is here, bringing illusions into the mix. Not everything is what it seems. If you are not careful, you may mistake longing for destiny, nostalgia for wisdom, deception for divine intervention.

entries.text: Venus begins her retrograde Aries and Pisces on March 1, dragging you through the past, not just through old relationships, but through old versions of yourself. This is about what you once desired, what you once believed you deserved, and the trade-offs you made along the way. The last time Venus retrograded here was March-April 2017.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Did you compromise on your professional worth? Then, on March 11, Venus slides back into Pisces. This is the love that never fully arrived. The sacrifice that never fully made sense. The dream that never quite came true. Pisces is your ninth house, and here, Venus is looking for meaning in love, but in retrograde, she is questioning everything. If you’ve romanticized the past, an old flame, an old dream, an old “what if”; this retrograde forces you to confront whether that fantasy ever had roots in reality. This is about self-worth. About the trade-offs you've made. About what you once believed you deserved.

entries.text: By the Virgo Eclipse on March 14, the focus sharpens: What is the story you tell yourself every day? What mental loops need to be broken? Communication and relationships with siblings or extended family may require a shift. The way forward is through rewriting the narrative.

entries.text: This Pisces season is not gentle. It does not warm you like the Sun. It does not stroke your ego or reward your confidence. It dissolves. It erodes. It pulls you into the places you have avoided, the debts, the obligations, the hidden agreements your soul has made. This season floods your eighth house, the underworld of intimacy, shared resources, power, and loss. You are standing in the liminal now, face-to-face with what you owe, not just financially, but karmically. The Pisces New Moon on February 27 is a moment of clarity. What is left unfinished? What patterns keep cycling through your relationships, your fears, your intimacy? The fears you keep buried, the debts that linger from past choices, the wounds that keep reopening, you cannot ignore them now.

entries.text: Venus retrograde begins March 1, setting fire to the past in the house of the future. Aries rules your ninth house—belief systems, long-term visions, the maps you make for your life. Venus does not move forward here; she moves in reverse, dragging her fingertips across the memories, retracing the places where desire first took root.
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.text: Have you been romanticizing a past version of yourself? Have you been chasing a dream that no longer fits, a vision of the future shaped by old expectations? This retrograde does not ask politely. It demands. Before you move forward, you must confront what still haunts you. The past is not gone; it lingers in the choices you make now, in the beliefs you hold onto like anchors when they were always meant to be driftwood. Venus is walking a path you walked eight years ago. March 2017. Who were you back then? Who did you love? What did you crave? And more importantly, what did you compromise to get it?

entries.text: Venus begins her descent in Aries on March 1, moving backward through your eighth house—power, intimacy, debts unpaid. This is where bonds are forged in fire, where love is not a feeling but a contract. The eighth house is where things are taken, where things are given, where something is always owed. Have you been settling for less than you deserve? Have you given too much for too little in return? Or worse, have you mistaken sacrifice for love? The last time she walked this path was March 2017. The past is not behind you, it lives in the fine print of the choices you made then. What were you learning about love, about power, about the cost of devotion? Where did you place your worth? What did you let slip through your fingers?

The one that lived more in your mind than in your hands. You can either be drown in the illusion, or start swimming.

entries.text: Venus retrograde begins in Aries on March 1, moving through your second house—money, stability, self-worth, survival. This is not the Venus of romance or pleasure. This is the Venus of what sustains you, what you rely on, what you believe you are owed. In Aries, Venus demands. She does not ask. She does not soften herself to be more acceptable. But when she is retrograde, her fire turns inward. The urgency does not fade; it simply circles. And here, in the second house, the question is sharp: What have you accepted as truth about your own worth? What have you settled for, not out of love, but out of fear? You have been here before. Look back to March 2017. A cycle is completing itself. Or maybe it is reopening. What were you learning then? About love? About money? About how you give yourself away?

entries.text: This lunation is the axis of Gemini and Sagittarius. The tension between information and insight. It pits facts against faith, data against belief, local against global. If Gemini asks, “What do I know right now?” Sagittarius replies, “But what does it mean in the bigger picture?”

entries.text: The signs Gemini and Sagittarius represent different methods of absorbing information and gaining an understanding of the world. The Gemini/Sagittarius polarity is associated with learning, collecting, and assimilating information. As Sagittarius observes the big picture, the sandbox Gemini focuses on the details that make up that picture, the grains of sand. In both cases, the objective is the same: to find the truth. The Gemini Sun collects information. The Sagittarius Moon questions meaning. And when they oppose each other, as they do now, we’re pressed to answer a core question: What do you still claim to believe, and does your life reflect that belief?

entries.text: In astrology, Gemini & Sagittarius represent the Third House of communication and the Ninth House of truth, forming an axis of the mind. Through this axis, you gain a clearer perspective on your life purpose and a deeper understanding of it. During this Full Moon, we have the chance to reflect on our soul's journey and story, asking ourselves, "What story do I want to tell about my life?" Now’s the time to reclaim authorship. To speak the truth you've been editing out. To let go of the limiting narratives that shrink your potential. This is about choosing. Choosing meaning. Choosing direction. Choosing yourself. Use this Full Moon to release the limiting stories you tell yourself, making way for great spiritual and mental expansion.

entries.text: Mars in Leo and the energy is raw, unfiltered. With Eris also present, that energy might feel explosive. You may feel the urge to quit, confront, escape, or sever. Don’t suppress the impulse. But don’t let it run you, either. Mars is a blade. In the right hands, it clears a path. In the wrong ones, it cut ties to the lifeline you still need. If you feel restless, don’t numb it. Move. Walk. Stretch. Create. Speak. If you feel angry, trace it to the truth underneath. Don’t waste it on someone who’s just a mirror.

Chiron pulls up old fears around being too loud, too direct, too much. But too much for who? Saturn in Aries is moving through your first house, quietly reshaping your sense of identity. Let this be a course correction, not a collapse.

entries.text: The Full Moon lands in your eighth house, where your deepest entanglements live, emotional, financial, energetic. Eris in this hidden space, awaken what you've buried, anger you weren’t allowed to feel, grief you never had time to name, instincts you learned to doubt to survive. Chiron points to past betrayals that made you self-protect first, connect second. This lunation brings an opportunity to release what no longer feel mutual and to trust your ability to rebuild from a stronger emotional foundation. You deserve more than survival. Saturn in Aries is asking you to look at the hidden patterns shaping your choices. Over the next six months, you’ll release more than you hold. Let what ends make space for what heals.

Eris may trigger tensions where you’ve been overlooked or undervalued socially. Chiron brings up that old ache of not being chosen, of having to earn your seat at the table, and how this might still influence who you trust. This lunation gives you the perspective to name what feels unbalanced. Saturn in Aries moves through your eleventh house too, asking for integrity in your long-term goals and the company you keep. Over the next six months, your connections will either deepen through shared purpose, or dissolve to make space for alignment.

Chiron reveals how your drive to be dependable was built in the aftermath of being left to figure it out alone. This lunation invites you to pause and reevaluate what’s sustainable. Mars makes you push harder. Saturn in Aries moves through your tenth house too, helping you build a reputation based on truth, not performance. Over the next six months, you’re redefining what success feels like, not what it looks like.

Eris may bring frustration around how often you’ve felt your ideas were too much or too far-reaching. Chiron here suggests an old wound around feeling out of place in academic, spiritual, or philosophical spaces. This lunation asks you to reclaim joy without explanation. Saturn in Aries is asking you to commit to your growth, not just fantasize about it. The next six months demand that you take your joy seriously. Stop downplaying what lights you up.

entries.text: The Full Moon lights up your second house of money, worth, and what you truly value. Opposite the Sun in your eighth, this lunation stirs up questions around shared resources, energetic entanglements, and the debts (emotional or financial) you’ve carried too long. Mars in Leo intensifies pressure at work. While Eris reminds you of the hidden toll of saying yes too often, charging too little, or tying your value to constant output. Chiron here speaks to the wound of needing to prove you’re useful to be loved. Saturn in Aries calls for discipline, not in service to others, but in service to your own well-being. Over the next six months, let value be something you live, not just something you chase. Live like you know yours.

entries.text: The Full Moon in your first house shines a light on your identity, your presence, and the pieces of yourself you've outgrown. Eris challenges the part of you that stays small to be accepted. Chiron surfaces the wounds around being “too much.” Too loud, too soft, too honest, too you. This lunation invites you to witness yourself without apology. With Saturn in your fifth house, you’re being called to commit to your own light. Over the next six months, shape a life that reflects your truth, not a version edited for someone else’s comfort.

Eris surfaces the unresolved tension buried in your foundation. Chiron in the fourth suggests that your definition of home may still be entangled with old pain. entries.text: Today we welcome the Summer Solstice in the Northern Hemisphere. The Sun enters Cancer, and we welcome Cancer Season. The Moon moves into Taurus today too, encouraging us to stay grounded. Eat some good food, breathe deeper, and listen to your body. You don’t need to earn rest, it’s part of what should be the natural process.

entries.text: The Summer Solstice marks the longest day of the year, a turning point where light peaks, then slowly begins its descent. As the Sun enters Cancer, we’re invited to shift from doing to feeling. The energy encourages you to come home to yourself. Let softness lead. Let care become your compass.

entries.text: Cancer is the sign that rules the home, family, and emotional safety. This season brings up themes around protection, nurturing, and belonging. It’s a time to care for yourself and the people who matter most. You may notice old memories or family dynamics resurfacing, this is a good time to reflect, not judge. Often, we repeat unconscious patterns until we decide to work through them. The goal here isn’t to blame, but to break cycles that no longer work for you.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Cancer is the Queen of the zodiac, a gently nurturing Universal mother that creates a safe space. Her energy and teachings help you to access deeper capacities for unconditional love. This is also an ideal time to help heal family dynamics. Often, the Universe will ask us now to face childhood memories that may still be shaping our choices, or quietly working against our growth.

entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: This is also a good time to focus on your home life, and foundation. Whether that means reconnecting with loved ones, establishing healthier habits, or setting boundaries, the focus is on creating emotional stability that supports your ability to take risk.

entries.text: The truth is: without a sense of safety, especially in your home or closest relationships, success becomes harder to sustain. You might still achieve, but at a cost. Chronic stress, burnout, or constant self-doubt often trace back to environments where emotional needs were ignored, dismissed, or unsafe to express. When you’ve had to stay alert just to feel safe, it becomes difficult to trust your own needs, rest when you need to, or ask for support.

entries.text: I see this pattern often: people pushing harder and harder to succeed, while silently feeling disconnected, unsupported, or exhausted. And when we trace it back, it’s not a lack of discipline or ambition. It’s the lack of foundation. Cancer Season offers you a chance to rebuild that foundation. you can start with where you are now. You can start by telling yourself the truth about what feels supportive and what doesn’t.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: So as the light begins to slowly wane, take this time to reset. You don’t need to push harder. You don’t need to prove anything. The strongest growth begins at the roots. This season is your invitation to strengthen yours.

June 22, 2025 – Sun square Saturn
This is a day when inner pressure can build. You may feel torn between showing up for others and tending to your own emotional needs. Saturn brings responsibility, structure, and high expectations. The Sun in Cancer asks you to check in with your heart. If you’re feeling stuck or heavy, try not to interpret it as failure. It may simply be a sign to pause, simplify, and clarify your priorities. Focus on what feels essential. Respect your emotional capacity.

June 23, 2025 – Sun square Neptune
This aspect can feel like walking through fog. Doubt, confusion, or emotional fatigue may surface. If you’re unclear about what’s real or what to do next, that’s okay. You’re not meant to have all the answers today. Let this be a reminder to protect your boundaries and step back from over-giving. Return to your body, drink water, limit screen time, and rest. Clarity comes when you stop trying to force understanding and start listening instead.

You might feel an undercurrent of intensity today. Something small may stir a much deeper reaction. This is an opportunity to notice where you’re holding control too tightly or avoiding vulnerability. Emotional defenses that once served you may now be getting in the way of deeper connection. You don’t have to fix anything immediately. Let your awareness grow first. Adjust your approach gently. Growth often begins with noticing.

entries.text: Everything begins at home, and if your nervous system is on edge, nothing else can truly settle. With Jupiter and the Sun moving through your fourth house, you’re being asked to examine the ground you stand on. What makes you feel safe? The Cancer New Moon hands you a blank page to rewrite your relationship to safety, belonging, and emotional truth. Mars in Virgo energizes your sixth house, helping you create daily rituals support the emotional repair work you’re doing. Mercury in Leo calls attention to your creativity and reminds you that creativity is part of your healing. The Capricorn Full Moon brings your public life into focus. What you build outward must be supported inward. You shouldn’t have to freeze your eggs because your job destroys your personal life. Can you choose stability that doesn’t come at the cost of your well-being, and family life?

entries.text: This season is here to help you get clear on how you think, what you believe, and the way you talk to yourself. With Jupiter in your third house, your mind is expanding, but Cancer Season is a reminder to be present, not just busy. If your thoughts have been looping, this is your invitation to calm them. The Cancer New Moon supports a fresh start in how you express yourself and how you let others hear you. Mars in Virgo brings energy to your creativity and reminds you that your joy matters just as much as your responsibilities. Mercury in Leo opens the door for real conversations at home. Speak honestly, especially with the people who matter most. The Capricorn Full Moon might bring up old beliefs or ideas that you’ve outgrown. This is your time to rewrite the story you’re living by, and making sure the voice in your head isn’t a false friend.

entries.text: This season is about coming back to what really supports you. With Jupiter and the Sun in your second house, things like money, time, energy, and self-worth are taking center stage. Cancer Season is here to remind you that real security comes from actually meeting your needs, without guilt. Mars in Virgo helps you clear out what’s not working at home or in your daily routine, so you can focus on what matters. Mercury in Leo helps you speak up with more confidence, especially when it comes to asking for what you need. The Capricorn Full Moon might shine a light on emotional or financial situations that have been slowly wearing you down. This is your reminder: your value isn’t something you have to prove by burning out. It comes from the choices you make to protect your peace. Start choosing you.

entries.text: This is your season to claim your space. With the Sun and Jupiter in your sign, everything expands: your growth, your needs, and your sense of what’s possible when you stop apologizing for taking up room. Cancer Season is not just a return. It’s a rebirth. The New Moon in your sign is a full-body reset, asking you to redefine who you are and what you’re no longer available for. Mars in Virgo activates your third house, sharpening your words and giving you the courage to say what you mean. Mercury in Leo highlights your worth. Speak from a place that remembers what you deserve. The Capricorn Full Moon puts your relationships in check. Who respects how far you’ve come, and who’s still treating you like a child.

entries.text: This is a season of letting go. With Jupiter and the Sun moving through your twelfth house, Cancer Season is drawing you inward to finally feel what you’ve been avoiding. It’s time to rest what’s been overworked, release what’s been weighing on you, and make space for what’s next. The Cancer New Moon gives you permission to reset and grieve whatever no longer belongs in your body or your story. Mars in Virgo brings energy to your second house, helping you rebuild your routines in a way that feels solid and nourishing. This is about care. Mercury moves into your sign, giving you the voice to express what’s been stuck. Say it clearly, but gently. The Capricorn Full Moon highlights burnout in your work or health routines. You don’t need to keep proving yourself. You need to heal. Let rest be enough.

entries.text: This is a season to get real about the future you're building, and who you’re building it with. With Jupiter expanding your eleventh house, your vision is big, your hopes are bigger, and you’re being reminded that you don’t have to do it all alone. But collaboration without a shared vision is an argument waiting to happen. The Cancer New Moon is your chance to reset your goals and reconnect with people who reflect your values. Mars in your sign gives you energy and focus, but be selective. Not every fire needs your attention. Mercury in Leo encourages you to listen to your gut before you speak or act. Some things are better processed in quiet first. The Capricorn Full Moon shines a light on your joy. Where have you put it on hold to be responsible? Your future starts when you stop settling and start believing you're worthy of more.

entries.text: This is a season to lead from truth. Jupiter is expanding your tenth house of purpose, visibility, and legacy. Cancer Season wants your outer life to match your inner values. If your work is out of alignment, this is your signal to fix things. The Cancer New Moon offers a reset in your public identity and professional purpose. Mars in Virgo fuels quiet inner work, helping you declutter emotional baggage and subconscious habits that shape how you show up. Mercury in Leo activates your eleventh house, reconnecting you with supportive allies and long-range vision. The Capricorn Full Moon highlights what your home, family, or past still influences. You do not need to carry outdated definitions of achievement. This season teaches you to build from authenticity. Leadership starts inside.

entries.text: This season is about expanding what you believe is possible without abandoning what keeps you grounded. Jupiter is opening your ninth house, asking you to stretch into a bigger vision for your life. Cancer Season invites you to pursue what nourishes your spirit, not just your ambition. The New Moon is a moment to recommit to what matters: your faith, your path, your voice. Mars in Virgo brings focus to your future and who is coming with you. Mercury in Leo amplifies your leadership and calls you to speak with conviction. The Capricorn Full Moon reveals the mindset that keeps you small or guarded. Let it go. Growth is not just what you learn. It is how you live. Choose meaning. Let your direction come from clarity, not escape.

entries.text: This season invites you to be with what you usually avoid. With Jupiter expanding your eighth house, emotional intensity rises to the surface. Cancer Season pulls you inward, asking you to explore the parts of your life you usually keep private. This is a time to look at what you’ve inherited, what you’ve merged with, and what you're finally ready to let go of. If you've been avoiding grief, this is your call to slow down and let it move. The New Moon offers a reset around intimacy, trust, and shared power. Mars in Virgo directs your attention to your public life and leadership responsibilities. This is a reminder to lead from your truth, not from obligation. Mercury in Leo gives you the tools to name what you're processing. Share it or keep it sacred if it needs more time. The Capricorn Full Moon shines a light on your financial values and boundaries. Use it to release scarcity stories or obligations that keep you locked in survival mode.

entries.text: This season is a mirror. Jupiter is expanding your seventh house, spotlighting your partnerships and asking you to show up more honestly in how you relate. Cancer Season is about seeing others clearly without losing sight of yourself. The Cancer New Moon offers a chance to reset your dynamics, especially in partnerships that have felt off-balance. Mars in Virgo brings clarity to your long-term goals and helps you prioritize emotional alignment over obligation. Mercury in Leo sharpens your communication around trust, intimacy, and shared resources. The Capricorn Full Moon lands in your sign, illuminating the ways you've grown and where you’re ready to lead differently. This season teaches you that deep love starts with deep truth. And that means showing up authentically, not just reliably.

entries.text: This is a season to come back into your body. Jupiter in your sixth house expands your attention to daily rhythm, wellness, and the systems that support your life. Cancer Season reminds you that your daily rituals need to be sacred. The New Moon offers a reset in how you care for your body, how you handle stress, and how you create order that holds you. Mars in Virgo helps you cut ties with draining agreements and shared responsibilities that no longer serve your healing. Mercury in Leo activates your one-on-one connections. Use it to speak from clarity, not control. The Capricorn Full Moon reveals the unconscious patterns that quietly drive your choices. You don’t have to prove your worth through output. You just need to start listening to what your body already knows. Release the burden. Begin again.

entries.text: This season calls you to create, connect, and care about what brings you back to life. Jupiter is expanding your fifth house of joy, pleasure, and self-expression. Cancer Season asks you to stop treating your joy like a reward and start treating it like a need. The New Moon offers a creative and emotional reset. What makes you feel free? Mars in Virgo brings focus to your relationships, refining who you share your energy with. Mercury in Leo calls you to realign your daily life with your values. The Capricorn Full Moon reveals where future goals are either aligned or outdated. Choose what makes you feel seen. This season teaches you that joy is not the reward for healing. It is part of the healing. Make space for what lights you up. And trust that it’s enough.

entries.text: We're building toward Eclipse Season. The Virgo Eclipse Season arrives as medicine for the part of you that believes criticism is care. This is a universal intervention for where self-improvement has become a type of self-destruction. Where impossible standards have become your prison, where you fix everything except your own exhaustion.

entries.text: This week's astrology: Venus enters Leo on Monday and immediately starts making moves. Five major Venus aspects in three days: your relationships, creativity, and values are getting reworked whether you're ready or not. Saturn retrograde in Pisces (since July 13) has been reviewing your spiritual boundaries, asking what illusions you've been maintaining in the name of compassion. When Venus in Leo shakes hands with Saturn, you get passion with staying power, if it's built on truth.

entries.text: Monday's Venus-Saturn trine asks you to stop treating commitment like restriction. The relationships worth having need daily tending, not grand gestures. By evening, Venus connects with Uranus - that thing you've been wanting to try but thought was "too much"? It's not. Uranus in Gemini wants intellectual rebellion, unexpected conversations, connections that surprise you. With Mercury about to enter Virgo (September 2), your mind is preparing for precision. Use this Venus-Uranus sextile to experiment before Virgo season's analysis kicks in.

entries.text: Tuesday brings the Venus-Neptune trine's intoxicating fog, but don't get too comfortable in the fantasy. Neptune retrograde in Aries has been reviewing where you've been spiritual bypassing instead of taking spiritual action. The dream feels beautiful, but Venus opposes Pluto by nightfall, dragging every unspoken resentment and power imbalance to the surface. If you've been pretending everything's fine while silently keeping score, the truth is about to emerge. Pluto retrograde in Aquarius doesn't do surface-level anything. This opposition exposes the collective shadows in your personal relationships.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Wednesday's Uranus-Neptune sextile creates a bridge between revolution and vision. The impossible suddenly has a blueprint. Your weird idea? It might actually work. This is the last major aspect before we enter the Eclipse portal.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Thursday's Moon in Scorpio sextile Sun in Virgo brings emotional depth to support practical action. After three days of Venus aspects exposing what's real versus what's performance, you finally have the emotional bandwidth to do something about it. This is integration day. Take what Venus revealed about your values and relationships and create one concrete change. Maybe it's a conversation you've been avoiding. Maybe it's a boundary you need to set. The Scorpio Moon gives you the courage, while Virgo Sun ensures it's practical, not dramatic.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Friday's Moon in Scorpio trine Jupiter in Cancer offers deep emotional support. This is the universe saying: "Yes, you can trust what you're feeling." After a week of revelations and confrontations, Jupiter provides the safety net. The feelings emerging now aren't random; they're signaling what needs healing before the Eclipse. Notice what makes you feel genuinely supported versus what's just familiar. Write down three things that actually nourished you today. You'll need this list when the Eclipse asks you to choose between comfort and growth.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: By Saturday, the Moon enters Sagittarius and emotions finally lighten. Scorpio showed you the depths; Sagittarius shows you the meaning. This is when the week's lessons start forming a coherent story. What pattern do you see? What's the common thread between Monday's Venus-Saturn commitment test, Tuesday's Venus-Pluto power dynamics, and Wednesday's breakthrough vision? The story you tell yourself on Saturday becomes the foundation you'll stand on when Eclipse Season arrives.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Sunday's First Quarter Moon in Sagittarius at 8:17 AM EST marks the first challenge to your Virgo New Moon intentions from August 23rd. Whatever daily practice or sacred routine you committed to is meeting its first test: Can it expand beyond perfectionism? The Moon's sextile to Mars in Libra adds courage to expand beyond comfortable limits. Your practical plans need a bigger vision. Don't abandon the practice because it's not perfect. Adjust it. Make it sustainable. The Eclipses will take whatever isn't working, but they'll strengthen whatever is genuine. This First Quarter Moon is your chance to refine before the universe does it for you.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: And this refinement matters, because Eclipse Season is almost here. Eclipse Season actually begins about two weeks before the first eclipse. By the time we hit September's Full Moon, we're already in the portal. The energy is already shifting. The old rules don't apply.
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.text: The September 7th Total Lunar Eclipse in Pisces will illuminate where perfectionism might have become too heavy to carry. Remember the Virgo New Moon from August 23rd? Whatever seeds were planted then, whether you set intentions or simply lived your daily life, because we're always planting through our thoughts and choices, will meet a moment of truth. This isn't a regular Full Moon where we release with candles and crystals. This is an Eclipse, which works differently: it clears what's complete and brings what's needed, often in unexpected ways.
entries.author: Marie Satori
entries.provenance: Published article body preserved by packages/astro-knowledge/voice/tldr-astro/fixtures/sky-article-longform/owner-corpus/manifest.json; voice evidence only, never runtime facts.

entries.text: Then comes the September 21st Partial Solar Eclipse at 29° Virgo: the final degree, the completion point. This will be the second Virgo New Moon this season (a rare occurrence), and at the anaretic degree, it's forcing completion of YEARS of Virgo themes: criticism, perfectionism, the belief that worth comes from usefulness and output.
entries.author: Marie Satori

entries.text: This week's Venus aspects aren't happening in isolation. They're preparation. Venus in Leo is teaching you to value yourself before the Eclipses strip away false validation. The Venus-Saturn trine builds foundations before the Eclipse dismantles unstable structures. By the time Mercury enters Virgo on September 2nd, followed by Uranus stationing retrograde on September 6th (one day before the Eclipse), the cosmic weather will have completely shifted. What you're building with Venus this week needs to be authentic, because the Eclipses will test everything that isn't.

entries.text: Stop trying to perfect your way to peace (Virgo shadow). Stop escaping into beautiful illusions (Pisces shadow). This week's Venus aspects are showing you where to find genuine value, sustainable love, and creative expression that doesn't require applause to exist.
