entries.text:
We bring a creative pursuit into the open and invite friends to take part. What felt like a small pleasure can become the plan everyone wants to join before we know whether we can sustain it. As Jupiter enters Leo, we grow through visible self-expression, big-hearted generosity, and the confidence to risk a larger stage. Once praise starts coming, we commit more time, make bolder promises, and give the idea more room.

We feel the pressure when we begin judging the pursuit by the attention it receives. Jupiter expands whatever is already in motion, not only what deserves more room. Creative courage and inflated ego can grow together, until every setback threatens to become a drama. The desire does not need to shrink. The work is to keep sharing the thing without making the recognition the reason we stay. Once excitement settles into routine, we find out whether we are building a meaningful practice or only chasing applause.

entries.text:
Opening: After moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, Jupiter enters Libra on {{entryDate}}. Jupiter governs growth, opportunity, and the confidence to reach for more than what already exists. Libra is the sign of balance, connection, and how we get along with each other. Together they make this a year where growth comes through who we meet and what becomes possible together: a friend's introduction leads to a creative collaboration, and the finished work reaches an audience neither person could have found alone. Jupiter spends about a year in each sign and takes about 12 years to visit all twelve.

Tension: Jupiter makes things bigger, and a few months in, the biggest thing is the list of what we have agreed to. Refusing feels rude, so we keep saying yes: another meeting, more of the work, another "it's fine" that is not true. Every extra request, correction, and follow-up starts going to the person who keeps saying yes. When a real choice comes up, we wait to hear what everyone else wants before saying what we want, and the decision goes to whoever speaks first. Somewhere along the way, being agreeable starts doing the work that honesty should be doing. The resentment stays quiet, because every one of these plans is something we technically agreed to.

Development: Jupiter last moved through Libra from {{previousResidencyEntryDate}} to {{previousResidencyExitDate}}, and whatever was learned about fairness then gets its next round now. Just because nobody has complained does not mean an arrangement is fair. This year it helps to say what changed early: that Saturday does not work, that the effort stopped being even, that one voice keeps making the decisions. Some connections will get closer once that is said plainly. Others end when the person benefiting from the old agreement is asked to do more.

Close: Before {{exitDate}}, we can quit one recurring commitment we have been keeping only because saying no feels rude.

Try this:
- We can answer one pending invitation with a clear yes or no instead of another maybe.
- We can say which day works for us before asking what everyone else prefers.
- We can stop sending reminders for a responsibility that belongs to someone else.

entries.text:
Opening: Mercury enters Pisces on {{entryDate}}, and ordinary conversations may carry more in the pauses than in the sentences. Someone reads a reply twice and says the tone does not match the words; after sitting with that feeling, we finally ask the useful question: “Did the answer change?” That sensitivity can catch a mixed signal before we act on it. Mercury moves through all twelve signs in about 1 year because it stays near the Sun. It usually spends roughly 2 weeks to 2 months in each sign, and a retrograde in that sign can extend the stay.

Tension: The trouble begins when the feeling itself gets treated as the answer. A pause sounds like refusal to one of us and uncertainty to another, but nobody checks. We soften a reply to avoid pressing, the next response stays just as vague, and we act on a decision that was never made. Everyone can explain what the exchange felt like, while the facts remain unsettled.

Development: Clarity now needs a small amount of structure, not a demand that every thought arrive fully formed. We can return to the exact words, say what we think we heard, and ask one plain question: “Was that a no, or is this still undecided?” Then a short message can state what we understood and what remains open. If the answer changes the story, we revise the decision. If no clear answer arrives, we leave it undecided instead of filling the silence ourselves.

Close: Before {{exitDate}}, we can reopen one unsettled exchange and ask for the answer we have been trying to infer.

Try this:
- We can reread one confusing message and copy the exact sentence that is shaping our interpretation.
- We can send “Still deciding” instead of another maybe that could be read as yes or no.

entries.text:
Opening: When Mars enters Libra on {{entryDate}}, the song we have been shaping with a collaborator has several endings and no final version. One ending hits harder; another fits the rest of the song better, and we keep revising so neither preference is overruled. The care is useful: a choice made with attention to another response can become sharper than a solo decision. Mars usually spends roughly 6 to 7 weeks in each sign and takes about 2 years to move through all twelve signs. A retrograde can extend one sign stay to about 7 months.

Tension: Before the next rehearsal, we send another edit, ask for another reaction, and soften the strongest moment before anyone can object. Neither of us says which ending we actually want. No argument happens, but the song stays unfinished, and each of us starts resenting the other for a delay both of us are creating. The same social awareness that protects the partnership now keeps either side from taking a clear position.

Development: At the next rehearsal, we stop making new edits and play the existing endings aloud. We each say which version we prefer and why. One concern exposes a weak transition, so we fix it; the other is simply disappointment that a favorite version will not win. We choose the stronger ending, and the remaining rehearsal goes toward timing and delivery instead of reopening the decision.

Close: Before {{exitDate}}, we can leave one shared choice settled even if someone involved is still disappointed by it.

Try this:
- We can replace one automatic “either is fine” with the option we actually prefer.
- We can send one reply we have been softening, using a clear sentence without adding an apology.
- We can make one visual or musical choice this week without collecting extra opinions.

Opening: From {{entryDate}}, a community class that once handed out a page of notes starts sharing the same lesson as a voice note, a short video, and a searchable transcript. A missed session no longer means losing the thread; someone asks a question in the daily message chain, another explanation appears, and the class starts teaching itself in several forms. This change has time to reshape habits rather than pass as a brief novelty. Uranus in Gemini takes about 84 years to move through all twelve signs and stays about 7 years in each sign.

Tension: The pressure builds when every new format promises to be quicker or clearer than the one already in use. The class moves from one thread to another, someone answers a difficult question with three more links, and an explanation gets abandoned when a fresher angle appears. The same willingness to experiment that made the lesson easier to access now scatters attention across unfinished versions. When a correction finally comes, the earlier wording is still being repeated, and the conversation changes subject before the mistake is settled.

Development: We do not need to defend the old handout or follow every new tool. We can keep the voice note that made the lesson easier to grasp, finish the explanation underneath it, and mark which claim changed after it was checked. If the message chain jumps to a new question, someone can return to the sentence left unanswered instead of adding another link no one has read. The chain gets quieter, and the corrected explanation is the one the class uses next time.

Close: Before {{exitDate}}, we can let one distracting format go.

Try this:
- We can finish one saved article or lesson before opening another tab on the same subject.
- We can return to one message thread and answer the question we skipped when the subject changed.
- We can compare one summary with its original source and correct one claim we repeated too quickly.

entries.text:
Mars enters Aries on {{entryDate}}, and waiting starts to feel worse than whatever happens next. The call gets made. The answer gets demanded. The part everyone has been circling finally has a name.

The problem is that relief can look a lot like certainty. Once the pressure breaks, every delay feels personal and every objection feels like something to defeat. We answer before we know what was actually said. We fix the first problem we can reach, even when it is not the one causing the damage.

Mars in Aries is good at beginning. It is less interested in cleaning up what happened because nobody stopped long enough to decide what they were trying to change. Before {{exitDate}}, notice which fight is moving the situation forward and which one is only giving the anger somewhere to go.
